# windows_iis_app_pool (Data Source)

Reads the observed state of an existing IIS application pool by `name` on a remote Windows host without managing it. Durations surface as whole minutes and `cpu.limit` thousandths as whole percent, converted server-side.

Requires IIS on the target host: install it with the `windows_feature` resource (`Web-Server`; add `Web-Mgmt-Console` / `Web-Scripting-Tools` for the `WebAdministration` module on Server Core).

Returns an error when the pool does not exist on the target host. The `SpecificUser` password is never returned.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Read the observed state of the DefaultAppPool (read-only, no lifecycle).
data "windows_iis_app_pool" "default" {
  name = "DefaultAppPool"
}

output "default_runtime" {
  value = data.windows_iis_app_pool.default.managed_runtime_version
}

output "default_state" {
  value = data.windows_iis_app_pool.default.state
}

# Inspect a pool managed by the windows_iis_app_pool resource in the same
# configuration. The data source returns the observed live state (durations
# as whole minutes, cpu.limit thousandths as whole percent).
data "windows_iis_app_pool" "managed" {
  name = windows_iis_app_pool.api.name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Application pool name on the target host.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `auto_start` (Boolean) Whether the pool starts automatically, as observed on the host.
- `cpu_action` (String) Action when the CPU limit is exceeded, as observed on the host.
- `cpu_limit_percent` (Number) CPU limit in whole percent, as observed on the host.
- `enable_32bit_app_on_win64` (Boolean) Whether 32-bit applications run on 64-bit Windows, as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Data source identifier: the application pool name.
- `identity_type` (String) Pool identity, as observed on the host.
- `identity_username` (String) Account for a `SpecificUser` identity, as observed on the host.
- `idle_timeout_action` (String) Action when the idle timeout elapses, as observed on the host.
- `idle_timeout_minutes` (Number) Idle timeout in whole minutes, as observed on the host.
- `load_user_profile` (Boolean) Whether IIS loads the user profile for the pool identity, as observed on the host.
- `managed_pipeline_mode` (String) Managed pipeline mode, as observed on the host.
- `managed_runtime_version` (String) CLR version, as observed on the host (`""` means No Managed Code).
- `max_processes` (Number) Maximum worker processes, as observed on the host.
- `queue_length` (Number) HTTP.sys request queue length, as observed on the host.
- `rapid_fail_protection` (Boolean) Whether rapid-fail protection is enabled, as observed on the host.
- `recycling_periodic_restart_minutes` (Number) Periodic restart interval in whole minutes, as observed on the host.
- `recycling_private_memory_kb` (Number) Private-memory recycle threshold in kilobytes, as observed on the host.
- `recycling_schedule` (Set of String) Daily recycle schedule (`HH:MM:SS` entries), as observed on the host.
- `start_mode` (String) Pool start mode, as observed on the host.
- `state` (String) Runtime state of the pool (`Started` / `Stopped`), as observed on the host.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
